claim: For the canonical minimal finite sphere models \(X_3=S^0\oplus S^0\oplus S^0\oplus S^0\) and \(X_2=S^0\oplus S^0\oplus S^0\), the compact-open finite mapping space \(\operatorname{Map}(X_3,X_2)\) has exactly \(738\) points and admits \(732\) successive Stong beat-point deletions, with \(128\) up-beat and \(604\) down-beat deletions, leaving exactly the six constant maps. The surviving subspace is canonically order-isomorphic to \(X_2\), has no beat points, and therefore is the core. Hence \(\operatorname{core}(\operatorname{Map}(X_3,X_2))\cong X_2\) and \(\operatorname{Map}(X_3,X_2)\simeq X_2\).

correctness.rationale: The exact finite claim is reconstructed from definitions. Exhaustive enumeration gives \(738\) monotone maps. A \(732\)-entry certificate is replayed point-by-point; \(128\) deletions satisfy the up-beat minimum condition and \(604\) satisfy the down-beat maximum condition in the current subposet. The six survivors are exactly the constant maps, their order is \(X_2\), and they have no beat points. The cited beat-point theorem then gives the asserted core and homotopy equivalence.

value.rationale: The core identifies the entire finite-space homotopy type, not merely the set of map-homotopy classes. The adjacent pair models the classical unstable problem \(S^3\to S^2\), whose mapping space has infinitely many components because \(\pi_3(S^2)\cong\mathbb Z\); the finite minimal models instead give a connected mapping space homotopy equivalent to \(X_2\). This makes the exact core a motivated boundary example and a reusable benchmark, rather than an arbitrary small-poset census.
